pages.title: What is UCYield?
pages.description: Understand the real-yield data infrastructure, its users, and the purpose of Shadow Ledger.

sections.title: A history you can verify
paragraphs: UCYield helps organizations turn operating data into verifiable records. Each record has a cryptographic identity; authorized parties can download its evidence and reproduce the result.
Shadow Ledger anchors that identity on Base Sepolia, adding a public point of comparison. Operating values remain encrypted off-chain.

rows: Record operating data and manage plants and record history.
Read and verify data for the plants they are allowed to access.
Reproduce results with the independent engine and CLI.

sections.title: Current scope
paragraphs: Phase 1 focuses on data infrastructure on Base Sepolia. UCYield Verified checks integrity and reproducibility; it does not establish whether a plant reported truthful operating values.
The older RWA/B20 issuance modules are retained as frozen reference code. Mainnet, payments, distributions, and funding rounds belong to separately gated work.

pages.title: Your first record
pages.description: Go from a data file to a verified record and downloadable evidence.

sections.title: Before you start
paragraphs: You need an issuer session, an active organization, and write access to a registered plant. Prepare monthly data and check the plant timezone.
Start with a completed month. Use a JSON file with schemaVersion 2.0.0, a matching plantCode, and registered metrics. Select the record type in the dashboard.

sections.title: Follow the workflow
list: Select the plant and record type, then upload the JSON file.
Review periods, metrics, and validation errors; confirm the record.
Wait for off-chain verification to complete.
If the record and plan are eligible, an IssuerAdmin authorizes anchoring with the embedded CDP wallet. The platform pays transaction fees.
Wait for finalized confirmation, then open the detail view and download the evidence bundle.

sections.title: Check the result
paragraphs: Read lifecycle, verification, anchoring, and integrity states separately. An internally committed record can be Verified without being Anchored.
Download the evidence and use /verify in the issuer dashboard. Chain comparison requires the CLI with an RPC connection and an independently confirmed ledger address.

pages.title: Shadow Ledger
pages.description: Distinguish internal data, the recordRoot identity, and anchoring evidence on Base.

sections.title: One identity for a record
paragraphs: recordRoot binds the header and every period in the record. The header includes source, plant, timezone, and registryHash; each period has its own salt.
The same document and salts yield the same recordRoot. Separate ingestions of identical values can produce different roots because salts and metadata differ.

rows: Document, source, salts, registry snapshot, seal, and log.
recordRoot, opaque references, metadata, and transaction evidence.

sections.title: Ledger v2 and v3
paragraphs: v2 uses period keys and a revision flow. v3 accepts independent records with overlapping months; the contract computes a periodSlot from organization, plant, record type, and month, then increments its anchor sequence.

Historical records must be verified against the correct ledger and bundle version. v3 source code does not confirm a v3 deployment; check configuration and deployment evidence before relying on v3 behavior.

pages.notice: Both v2 and v3 are present in source. A live v3 deployment was not confirmed during this review.

pages.title: Record lifecycle
pages.description: Read Committed, Verified, Anchored, and integrity states correctly.

rows: Confirm the record, create a seal, and append the log.
Progress and outcome of the verification request.
The complete finalized receipt and events have been matched.

sections.title: Wait for finality
paragraphs: Submitting a transaction does not make a record Anchored. A successful receipt and matching events at a finalized block are required.
After anchoring, the system verifies again with chain evidence. The earlier off-chain result and the on-chain result are distinct steps.

sections.title: Infrastructure errors and invalid evidence
paragraphs: An unavailable RPC, storage dependency, or trust configuration is not invalid evidence. The request remains Queued with an infrastructure code for recovery.

When automatic retries are exhausted, the interface indicates that retries stopped. Once the dependency recovers, re-verification creates a new request. Actual cryptographic contradictions produce Failed.

pages.title: Privacy & access
pages.description: Understand public chain data and operating data available only to authorized readers.

sections.title: What is public
paragraphs: EVM hashes, metadata, and transactions are publicly observable. Operating values, personal names, and credentials do not belong in calldata.
Per-period salts and opaque references reduce the ability to guess values from roots. They do not conceal all metadata or relationships between anchors.

sections.title: Operating values require authorization
paragraphs: Documents and source data are encrypted off-chain. The API checks organization, active membership, and plant scope before serving data or evidence.
Invited viewers can access only their granted plants. Knowing a recordId or a public transaction does not grant access to confidential data.

sections.title: Sharing evidence bundles
paragraphs: An evidence bundle can contain operating values, salts, and source material needed to recompute the root. Anyone receiving the file can read its contents.
Share bundles only with parties authorized to receive those values. Revoking API access cannot recall a previously downloaded file.

pages.title: Upload operating data
pages.description: Prepare JSON with a matching plant, calendar periods, and registered metrics.

sections.title: Currently accepted file format
paragraphs: The ingest endpoint accepts .json files up to 1,000,000 bytes. Select plantId and recordType in the dashboard; do not add a header or salts to the upload file.
The example uses a fictional plant. Replace plantCode with your real plant code and use metrics registered for its asset category.

sections.title: Validation rules
list: Use YYYY-MM periods, 1–12 periods per record, and no repeated period within a file.
Prefer decimal strings for metrics with a decimal point; no exponents or thousands separators.
Metric keys must be registered and satisfy precision and range constraints.
Do not repeat JSON keys or add fields outside the schema.

sections.title: Current month and provisional data
paragraphs: In ledger v3 mode, a record containing the current month at ingestion is provisional. It can be committed and verified off-chain but cannot be anchored.
Provisional status is fixed by ingestedAt and timezone. Ingest again after the month closes to create a new record; the old record does not become final merely with time.

pages.notice: CSV/XLSX and preview exist in library code / plans, but the inspected ingest endpoint accepts JSON only. Do not assume dashboard upload support.

pages.title: Connect a data source
pages.description: The Huawei FusionSolar flow, plant binding, and fetch outcomes.

sections.title: Connect and bind a plant
paragraphs: The provider flow uses server-managed credentials. Test the connection, choose a compatible mapping template, and bind the provider station code to the organization plant.
Keep passwords, tokens, and sensitive response content out of public documentation. Provider access and UCYield data access are separate scopes.

sections.title: Fetch monthly data
paragraphs: Authorized users can trigger a fetch or configure a schedule. The worker fetches the source, maps metrics, normalizes values, and creates records; the current fetch flow supports automatic off-chain commit.
An empty response or a month without values must not become zero. Inspect fetch outcomes to distinguish missing data, authentication problems, rate limits, and schema errors.

sections.title: Integration boundaries
paragraphs: Native Provider API, full source slicing/replay, and Huawei OAuth have separate specifications and plans. Publish them as usable features only after verifying their endpoints and interface flows.
This review inspected JSON upload and Huawei API-account fetch as the core paths. It does not certify a live provider connection or environment credentials.

pages.title: Members & plant access
pages.description: Assign appropriate access to administrators, operators, and invited viewers.

rows: Manage the organization and authorize eligible anchor batches.
Write records for plants with granted write access.
Read data and evidence for granted plants.

sections.title: Plant-scoped permissions
paragraphs: Membership does not grant access to every organization. The active session selects the organization; plant permissions determine readable and writable data.
Organization or plant status changes can invalidate an operation even if a button remains visible. The server rechecks authorization when executing.

sections.title: Give a reviewer access
paragraphs: Invite the viewer into the correct organization and grant only the plants they need. A viewer can download in-scope evidence for independent review.
Application roles and contract roles are different. A reader does not need issuer transaction signing authority.

pages.title: What does UCYield Verified mean?
pages.description: Reproducible checks, signed receipts, and the limits of the Verified claim.

sections.title: What the result means
paragraphs: UCYield Verified is the result of recomputation and evidence comparison, with a receipt signed by the verifier key. Authorized recipients can rerun the same engine.
The result protects integrity after commit. It does not establish the accuracy of a meter, revenue report, or values supplied by an issuer or provider.

rows: Parser/schema, canonical bytes, root, projection, source/registry, period identity, seal/log.
Also checks finalized commitment evidence and issuer wallet organization binding.
Signature, trusted key, evidence content, and record identity.

sections.title: Trust boundaries
paragraphs: Obtain the trust store independently from the bundle. Keys declared by the evidence file itself are not a sufficient trust foundation.
Under ADR-0031, the active product does not claim Chainlink DON, OracleConsumer, or Nitro attestation. Those descriptions belong to earlier designs.

pages.title: Verify evidence independently
pages.description: Download a bundle, choose an independent trust store, and run the browser verifier or CLI.

sections.title: Prepare evidence and trust
paragraphs: Download evidence from the detail view while authorized for the plant. A bundle includes document, source, registry snapshot, seal, log, and receipts, with an anchor when present.
Obtain trust independently, for example from /api/v1/public/verifier-keys on a trusted API or finalized ledger events. Confirm the ledger address through a separate trusted channel.

sections.title: Browser or CLI
paragraphs: The issuer dashboard /verify page runs evidence checks in the browser. It is the starting point for an authorized recipient.

Run the commands below from the ucyield monorepo checkout with dependencies installed. The verifier is currently a private workspace package; do not assume a public npm installation. The second command uses an RPC connection and the ledger matching the bundle.
sections.code:
pnpm --filter @ucyield/verifier ucy-verify \
  evidence.bundle.json --trust trust.json

pnpm --filter @ucyield/verifier ucy-verify \
  evidence.bundle.json --trust trust.json \
  --rpc "$BASE_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
  --ledger "$CONFIRMED_LEDGER_ADDRESS" --json

rows: Contradictory evidence or an invalid receipt.
Infrastructure / finality is unavailable, or CLI usage is invalid.

pages.title: Canonicalization & hashing
pages.description: ucy-hash-v2: canonical bytes, Merkle trees, salts, and recordRoot.

sections.title: From values to deterministic bytes
paragraphs: Canonical JSON uses compact UTF-8, code-point key sorting, and Unicode NFC normalization. Keys that collide after normalization are rejected. Optional fields are omitted rather than set to null.
Metrics are canonical decimal strings, without floating-point arithmetic. 370.10 normalizes to 370.1; exponent notation and unknown schema fields are rejected.

sections.title: Build the record identity
paragraphs: The D_* constants separate hash domains; each period salt is 32 random bytes. The formulas below are a schematic, not a substitute implementation.
periodCount is ABI-encoded as uint256. The Merkle tree uses OpenZeppelin StandardMerkleTree with bytes32 values and its double-hashing convention, including for a single period.
sections.code:
headerHash  = keccak256(utf8(canonical(header)))
dataHash_i  = keccak256(utf8(canonical({metrics, period})))
leaf_i      = keccak256(abi.encode(D_period, headerHash, dataHash_i, salt_i))
periodsRoot = StandardMerkleTree.of([[leaf_i]], ["bytes32"]).root
recordRoot  = keccak256(abi.encode(D_record, headerHash, periodsRoot, periodCount))

sections.title: What must be retained
paragraphs: Retain exact document bytes, source, salts, registry snapshot, and algorithm version. The uploaded metric file alone cannot reconstruct recordRoot because ingestion creates the header and salts.
A registry snapshot captured at ingestion lets historical records remain verifiable when the dictionary expands. Use repository golden vectors and the verifier engine to check compatibility.

pages.title: Shadow Ledger API
pages.description: A map of core endpoints; the full contract lives in the monorepo OpenAPI specification.

sections.title: Integration conventions
paragraphs: The API prefix is /api/v1. Private endpoints require authentication, with organization scope determined from the session rather than a client-supplied orgId.

Use Idempotency-Key for supported operations. Reusing a key with a different body yields IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE; matching requests replay their stored result. Zod and OpenAPI define authoritative bodies, responses, and errors.

rows: Confirm recordIds, append seal and log.

sections.title: Asynchronous operations
paragraphs: 202 Accepted means the request was accepted, not that its transaction is finalized. Observe batch and record states before reporting a successful anchor.
This map is an endpoint guide rather than a full API reference. Do not infer signing payloads, authentication headers, or responses from endpoint names.

pages.title: Smart contracts & versions
pages.description: Contract roles, commitBatch, markVerified, and ledger compatibility.

sections.title: Separate on-chain responsibilities
paragraphs: The contract uses AccessControl and ERC-2771. Issuer wallets are bound to orgRef; a relayer funds the transaction while valid forwarded calls retain issuer identity.
ISSUER_ROLE commits records; VERIFIER_ROLE records verification; CHECKPOINT_ROLE writes checkpoints. The admin manages roles and configuration. These roles are not API read permissions.

rows: Commit recordRoot identities subject to contract limits.
Anchor the Merkle root of organization log heads.
Bind a wallet to orgRef and grant issuer authority.

sections.title: Check the right address and version
paragraphs: Bundle v1 corresponds to ledger v2; current bundle v2 code supports ledger v3. v3 exposes periodAnchorCount and sequences for month-slot history.
Do not trust a ledger address merely because a bundle declares it. Independently confirm chainId, address, and deployment block; these docs do not assert a live v3 address.

pages.title: System architecture
pages.description: The monorepo components responsible for data, evidence, and transactions.

sections.title: From source to ledger
paragraphs: The issuer dashboard is the operating interface. The NestJS API coordinates ingestion and access; workers handle fetching, verification, relaying, indexing, and monitoring. PostgreSQL stores state and logs; source/documents are encrypted.

packages/hashing defines bytes and hashes. packages/verifier independently reproduces evidence. packages/contracts defines Zod/API contracts; packages/ingest contains pure parsers and mapping, with endpoint availability documented separately.

sections.title: Consistency during failure
paragraphs: State, audit, and outbox entries are written in the same transaction. Consumers record inbox receipts atomically with their effects so replay does not lose or duplicate work.

Chain writes follow reserve → sign once → persist raw transaction and hash → broadcast → resend the same transaction. Replacements/cancellations keep the nonce; finalized receipts determine the outcome.

sections.title: Package boundaries
paragraphs: Domain and pure engines do not depend on NestJS or the database. Applications wire adapters to use cases; packages never depend on an application.
Tests and CI use simulated adapters. Deployment and Base Sepolia smoke verification are separate gates; builds and tests do not prove the live environment has the intended configuration.

pages.title: Scope & roadmap
pages.description: Separate implemented flows, cutover-dependent capabilities, and future work.

sections.title: Phase 1 · Base Sepolia
paragraphs: The product focuses on operating records, cryptographic identity, verification, and permissioned selective disclosure. Phase 1 uses Base Sepolia, chainId 84532.
These guides were checked against the source checkout on 4 October 2026. No live smoke test or secret/deployment configuration inspection was performed for this documentation design.

sections.title: Further gates
paragraphs: A mainnet pilot depends on LegalReadinessGate and owner approval. Issuance, payments, distributions, and funding rounds cannot be inferred from data anchoring.
Update documentation when APIs change, ledger cutovers complete, or integrations pass deployment verification. A roadmap is not a launch confirmation.
